transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I came in because I just can't seem to shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It kind of feels like everything I managed to build back up after my divorce has just completely collapsed... and I'm just sitting under it. I just don't know how to get out from under it right now.
When did this heavy, hopeless feeling start — was it right after your divorce, or has it been building gradually over time?

Well, it wasn't exactly right after the divorce itself. Um... I'd say this feeling has been hanging over me for about a month now. It really started to hit when I had to deal with all the financial mess that came after everything was finalized.
Before the financial problems started a month ago, were you experiencing any of these heavy or hopeless feelings, or did they really only begin once you had to deal with that financial mess?
No, I wasn't. Um... it really only began once I had to face all the financial stuff. Before a month ago, I didn't feel hopeless like this at all. It really just started when that whole mess hit.
Over this past month, how has this feeling affected your ability to work, take care of yourself, or do your daily activities?

It's affected pretty much everything. At work, I was making some really questionable calls and just... falling apart in meetings. My supervisor actually had to step in and take me off all active project decisions. And at home, I just completely stopped keeping up with my basic routines. It got so bad that I actually ended up being sent to the emergency department... I just didn't feel safe with my own thoughts anymore.

Looking back before the financial problems started, over the weeks and months after your divorce was finalized, did you notice any gradual changes in your mood, energy, sleep, or ability to concentrate — even if they were subtle — or did you feel essentially back to normal until the financial mess hit?

Um... no, not really. After the divorce was finalized, I actually thought I was doing okay. I felt pretty much back to normal, honestly. I didn't notice any subtle changes in my sleep or my focus or... anything like that. It wasn't building up. I really just felt fine until all that financial stuff hit me a month ago.

When the financial problems hit a month ago, did your mood and these hopeless feelings come on suddenly — like within days — or did they gradually build up over the first week or two after you found out about the financial mess?

I'm honestly not sure. Um... it's a little hard to remember the exact timeline of those first few days. When I realized how bad the financial mess was, everything just kind of fell apart. I don't really know if the hopeless feelings hit me all at once right when I found out, or if it took a week or so to really build up and set in. It's all just kind of a dark blur right around that time.

When you first realized how bad the financial situation was, did the hopeless feeling and these other symptoms start within the first few days, or did it take a week or more before you really started feeling this way?

Like I was just saying, I really don't know. It's hard to separate those first few days from the rest of the week. I just don't remember exactly how fast it all hit me after I found out about the money. It's all just kind of blurred together.

Looking back, would you say that within the first 3 days after you found out about the financial mess, you were already feeling this hopeless and heavy feeling, or did you feel relatively okay for a few more days before it really hit you?

I... I really can't break it down like that. Like I said, I just don't have a timeline for you. I don't know if it was day two or day five. I just know I saw the accounts, and then... everything went dark. I honestly can't tell you if I was okay for those first three days or not.

Even if you can't remember the exact day, do you remember whether you felt okay enough to do your normal activities in those first few days after finding out about the money, or were you already struggling right away?

I just... I really don't remember. I don't know if I went to work or if I stayed in bed those first few days. I can't tell you if I was functioning or not. I'm sorry, I just don't have that information for you. It's just a blank.

In the week after you found out about the financial mess, do you remember having even one day where you felt like you could get out of bed and do something, or were you pretty much unable to function from the very beginning?

I just... I really don't know. Like I keep saying, that whole first week is just gone. I don't remember if I had a good day in there or if I was just completely out of it from the start. I just know it got bad, but I can't tell you exactly when or how it played out day by day.

Before you found out about the financial mess, in the weeks right after your divorce was finalized, did you notice any change in how you were sleeping — like sleeping more than usual, or having trouble falling asleep — even if it was subtle?

I'm not exactly sure when it started... if it was right after the divorce or later. But lately, my sleep has just been really bad. I either lie awake staring at the ceiling, just replaying all the bills and the mistakes I've made at work, or... or I wake up way before dawn, and I just feel like I never actually slept at all.

When you think back to right after your divorce was finalized — before you found out about the financial mess — do you remember your sleep being normal back then, or was it already disrupted at that point?

I really don't know for sure. I mean, the divorce was hard, obviously, but... I don't specifically remember if my sleep was already messed up then. It's just all kind of a blur until the money stuff hit, and then everything definitely got worse. But before that? I couldn't tell you if I was sleeping normally or not.

Looking back to the weeks right after your divorce was finalized, before the financial mess started, did you have any days where you felt sad or down, or did you genuinely feel okay emotionally during that time?

Right after the divorce was finalized... I mean, I think I was actually trying to keep things together. I felt like I was starting to build a new life. So I don't remember feeling completely down back then. 

But now... honestly, that's why I came in to see you. I just can't shake this really heavy, hopeless feeling. It feels like everything I built after the divorce has just completely collapsed, and I'm just... sitting under it all.

In the two weeks right before you found out about the financial mess, would you say you were feeling hopeful about rebuilding your life, or were you already starting to feel some heaviness or sadness creeping in?

I think I was still feeling hopeful. Or at least, I don't remember feeling sad yet. I was just trying to focus on work and getting things back on track. I really don't think the heaviness started until I actually found out about the money. Before that... I'm pretty sure I was doing okay.

In the month or two before you found out about the financial mess, did you ever feel like things were pointless or that nothing really mattered — even if it was just for a day or two — or did you feel like life had purpose and meaning during that time?

Back then, no, I really felt like my life had purpose. I was working and trying to move forward, so I didn't feel like things were pointless. 

It's really just... now. Like I was saying a minute ago, the reason I came in is because of how I feel right now. I just can't shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It really does feel like everything I tried to build after the divorce has completely collapsed, and I'm just sitting under it all. But a couple of months ago? No, I wasn't feeling like this yet.

When you think back to that day you found out about the financial mess, and then the next day or two after that — do you remember feeling the heaviness and hopelessness right away, or did it take several days or a week to really start feeling that way?

It hit me pretty much right away. As soon as I realized the extent of the financial mess... that's when it all just settled in. It's been hanging over me for about a month now, ever since that day, and it just hasn't lifted at all.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the onset of depression was truly sudden and clearly tied to the financial stressor (suggesting F43.21 Adjustment Disorder), or whether there were pre-existing depressive symptoms that the patient may not be fully recalling, which would suggest F32.9 Major Depressive Disorder
doctor.question: In the month or two before you found out about the financial mess, did you ever feel like things were pointless or that nothing really mattered — even if it was just for a day or two — or did you feel like life had purpose and meaning during that time?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I built after the divorce has collapsed and I’m just sitting under it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of pointlessness or lack of meaning/purpose prior to the financial mess, which relates to depressed mood (sad, empty, hopeless).

patient.answer:
Back then, no, I really felt like my life had purpose. I was working and trying to move forward, so I didn't feel like things were pointless. 

It's really just... now. Like I was saying a minute ago, the reason I came in is because of how I feel right now. I just can't shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It really does feel like everything I tried to build after the divorce has completely collapsed, and I'm just sitting under it all. But a couple of months ago? No, I wasn't feeling like this yet.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the onset of depressive symptoms was acute (within days of the stressor) or whether there was a gradual build-up over weeks, which would help differentiate between an adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.21) and major depressive disorder (F32.9).
doctor.question: When you think back to that day you found out about the financial mess, and then the next day or two after that — do you remember feeling the heaviness and hopelessness right away, or did it take several days or a week to really start feeling that way?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depression has been hanging over me for about a month, starting around the financial mess after the divorce.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the onset of the depressive symptoms (heaviness and hopelessness) in relation to the event (finding out about the financial mess), which relates to the duration and timeline of the depressive episode.

patient.answer: It hit me pretty much right away. As soon as I realized the extent of the financial mess... that's when it all just settled in. It's been hanging over me for about a month now, ever since that day, and it just hasn't lifted at all.

inference.note: Patient reports clear temporal relationship between identifiable stressor (financial mess discovery) and symptom onset within days. Symptoms hit 'pretty much right away' after the stressor. Pre-stressor functioning was normal with no prodromal symptoms. This acute onset in direct response to a specific stressor, with significant functional impairment and ED visit, is consistent with Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood (F43.21). The timeline and presentation do not support Major Depressive Disorder (F32.9), which would typically show more gradual onset or pre-existing mood symptoms.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with depressive symptoms (hopelessness, heaviness, functional impairment, sleep disturbance, suicidal ideation requiring ED visit) that emerged acutely within days of a clearly identifiable psychosocial stressor (financial crisis following divorce finalization). The temporal relationship between the stressor and symptom onset, the acute presentation, and the patient's explicit attribution of symptoms to the stressor are consistent with Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood. While major depressive disorder remains in the differential, the acute onset tied to a specific identifiable stressor and the one-month duration favor adjustment disorder. The diagnosis code F43.21 specifies Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood.
